findings.title: The theme name line names the hovered or focused chip instead of what is drawn
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured (Default, shared Void), key-custom-dim (own Ember), key-configured with theme 'neon-future' and shared Midnight; 373x410 DPR 1; task: which theme is this key showing and what does Default resolve to
findings.observed: Pointer over Graphite/Forest/Paper replaces 'Theme Default · Void' with 'Graphite'/'Forest'/'Paper' while Default stays checked and Void is drawn; during those hovers no visible text outside the chips names Void. With own Ember, hovering Default shows 'Default · Void' while Ember is drawn. With an unknown stored theme the line reads '"neon-future" · draws Void' at rest, then 'Default · Midnight' as soon as Tab lands on the Default chip (it holds the Tab stop unchecked) while the key face is Void (#000000) and the help line below still says 'draws Void'.
findings.evidence: MEASURED p1-theme.json; screenshots ev-hover-forest.png, ev-unknown-tab.png. READ pi-common.js: pointerover/focusin set previewTheme and renderThemeLine prefers it. The preview was built for the unnamed strip F; the named chips make it redundant. Breaks contract 1 (resolved theme visible without a tooltip) on every hover and REPORT.md's 'the line above says what is drawn'.
findings.affected_user: everyone using a pointer; keyboard users when a stored theme is unknown
findings.correction: Render the line from themeOverride only; remove the pointerover, focusin, pointerleave and focusout preview listeners (about 15 lines). Rewrite the e2e check that asserts the preview (X02).
findings.tradeoff: Loses a second copy of the pointed chip's name, which the chip already shows.
findings.acceptance_test: C1: key-configured 373x410, real pointer over each of the 8 chips then off the band: #theme-current is 'Default · Void' at every step, 'Void' visible outside the chips at every step, 0 writes. C2: theme 'neon-future' with shared Midnight, Tab into the gallery: the line names Void at rest and after Tab, 0 writes.

findings.title: Uncommitted text in the panel's own text fields is not saved on the leave signals
findings.area: Rotation rename (F2 field), group name field, detail list cell rename vs pi-shell.js pendingFlushes
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured, dial-groups, key-details at 373x410; control: Label on key-configured
findings.observed: Type 'Zzq' without Enter, then fire mouseleave on the root and blur on the window (the signals the shell relies on because pagehide saves never land, bench 2026-09-23): Label writes 1 frame with the text; the rotation rename, group name and cell rename write 0 frames and the text is not stored.
findings.evidence: MEASURED p8-d03.json. READ pi-shell.js 116-130: the leave flush covers only [data-setting] fields. Whether the real app's key switch fires change on these inputs before teardown is not known (INFERRED risk: the bench lost 20 of 20 quick Label edits before the leave flush existed).
findings.affected_user: everyone who renames a rotation member, a group or a detail cell and then clicks another key
findings.correction: Register these fields' commits with the shell's pendingFlushes set (same leave flush as bound fields), guarded against IME composition.
findings.tradeoff: A pointer leaving the panel mid-word commits the partial name (the Label already behaves so).
findings.acceptance_test: C7: simulator: each field writes exactly 1 frame containing the typed text after mouseleave + window blur. Real host: type a rename without Enter, click another key within 1 s, reselect the dial: the name is present in 5 of 5 tries.

own_regression_risks: X01: removing the hover preview drops a pointer cue; the e2e preview assertion must change in the same commit.
X02: tightening to === 1 fails on grouped rotation edits until they send one frame; merging the two frames risks the torn-pair bug class unless it copies the existing detailTilesStage pattern.
X03: reserving the wrapped toolbar height makes each grouped list 32 to 96 px taller at zoom widths; a wrapping hint adds a line.
X04: stacking the face below about 240 px makes the header taller there and moves the palette lower at those widths (the header is unpinned there already).
X05: shortening the Gadget info status puts the provider-link and stable-ID caveats behind a click; the one-line summary must keep 'no min, max or average' visible.
X06: swapping the rotation marks changes a learned visual, needs forced-colors parity kept, and invalidates docs screenshots.
X07: a leave flush on rename and group-name fields commits partial names when the pointer leaves mid-word; it needs the IME composition guard the bound fields have.
X08: a stricter first-screen metric makes old and new tables incomparable; publish both for one round.
X10: an Undo that survives other edits or a reload could restore stale state; keep it panel-local and clear it on any other edit.
